Thanks again for the call today, Adele — really useful discussion. Below is a concise recap and the immediate asks so we can scope a short POC for Private (VPC) deployment and validate performance SLOs.

Quick recap
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 latency <= 150ms for streaming responses (60–120 tokens), sustained throughput target ~400–600 req/s, and peak concurrency of ~50 simultaneous sessions.
- Workload: mostly short chat sessions, some longer generation for summaries (~350 tokens) but rare.
- Data residency requirement: Private VPC in us-east-1; no cross-region routing for inference traffic.

Primary unknowns we agreed to validate
1) Network path and egress: will traffic flow over an existing VPN or can we set up VPC peering/PrivateLink?
2) Internal latency budget: app -> inference endpoint RTT target (you suggested <8ms ideally) — need measurements from your app AZs to the prospective subnet.
3) Streaming vs non-streaming behavior: will you need server-sent events (streaming) with sub-50ms first-token latency for interactive UX?

Immediate asks / next steps
- Adele: share the network contact and attach the current VPC/network diagram (subnets, NAT, VPN/Transit Gateway, firewall appliance).
- NetOps: provide recent traceroutes from the app subnet to the candidate inference subnet, current MTU, IPSec/IKE profile if VPN, and any NAT timeouts.
- Redwood (we): send a concise test plan + checklist for network prerequisites and propose two 2-hour windows to run end-to-end perf runs.

Attached: redwood_private_deploy_network_checklist.pdf — a short checklist of ports, MTU expectations, and traceroute packet captures we need.

Proposed timeline
- Net info shared by EOD 2025-09-13
- Tech deep-dive with Solutions on 2025-09-15 (60 min)
- Perf POC run 2025-09-17/18 (2 hours)

If that looks good I’ll loop in Rishi and Vivek from our infra/solutions team to coordinate the deep dive and test plan.

Thanks for the ping — reviewed their diagram and initial targets. High-level technical notes and recommended test vectors below. I also attached a minimal test-plan markdown with packet captures/traceroute templates.

Summary assessment
- Streaming p95 <=150ms is achievable if we avoid cross-region hops and can keep app->inference RTT <8ms. With peering in the same AZ the platform can hit ~80–120ms p95 for 60–120 token streams (depends on model size and batching).
- VPN (IPSec) via a Transit Gateway often adds 10–30ms and jitter depending on encryption offload; if their VPN is appliance-based NAT + IPSec, expect additional CPU-induced latency under load. Recommend peering or PrivateLink where possible for <10ms extra latency.

Test vectors to validate (we should run all during POC windows):
1) Baseline RTT: ICMP + TCP handshake from app worker to target subnet (us-east-1a/b). Capture p50/p95/p99.
2) Traceroute (UDP and TCP) to identify hop counts and MTU blackholes.
3) Small streaming test: 1–2 tokens bursts to measure first-byte latency (server-send).
4) Sustained qps test: ramp to 400/500/600 rps for 10–15 minutes, monitor per-instance CPU, GPU utilization, and NAT/Firewall throughput.
5) Concurrency spike: 50 concurrent sessions with variable token lengths to observe queueing and p95 drift.

Network prerequisites checklist (from my perspective)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 and 80 from app subnets to inference subnets (we use TLS).
- UDP/ICMP allowed for traceroutes temporarily.
- MTU >= 1400 end-to-end to avoid fragmentation on gRPC/websocket streams.
- Keep NAT session timeouts > 30s for active streaming sessions.

Egress/cost note
- If traffic exits their VPC and re-enters via a co-lo or through a VPN appliance, they may incur additional data transfer charges and NAT appliance bandwidth limits. We should capture bytes/sec during the sustained run to estimate egress costs.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-test-plan.md (includes exact curl/grpc commands and a short load script).

I’ll prepare an infra estimate: approx 4 x A10G-ish instances for initial POC (depends on model) to satisfy 600 rps with streaming enabled; will firm up after we know model and token distribution.
